LanguageData.RWL_Quotes_Show: Show quotes in thoughts and log
LanguageData.RWL_Quotes_ShowTip: Thoughts and log entries made by a spoken line show the line itself.
LanguageData.RWL_Quotes_Vanilla: Voice the game's own social interactions
LanguageData.RWL_Quotes_VanillaTip: When two voiced colonists have a vanilla insult, slight, kind words, chat and so on, the mod writes the words for it. The game's own effects stay as they are.
LanguageData.RWL_LogCount: {0} of {1} lines (the log keeps the last {2}).
LanguageData.RWL_Share_FooterTip: Add the "RimWorldLLM: local AI colonist dialogue for RimWorld" footer to copied text and saved share images.
LanguageData.RWL_LogPawnGone: {0} is no longer in the game.
LanguageData.RWL_Refused_not_negative: listener had nothing to be comforted about
LanguageData.RWL_Refused_vanilla_interaction: the game already applied its own effect
LanguageData.RWL_Refused_stack_full: the listener already has this thought
LanguageData.RWL_ChronEmpty: The narrator has not written any chronicle entries yet.
LanguageData.RWL_MindNoMind: The agent has not built a mind for {0} yet. It appears once the agent has run for this pawn.
LanguageData.RWL_MindNoEvolvingBio: The bio has not changed yet.
LanguageData.RWL_MindNotesHint: Your notes to this pawn's mind. The agent keeps them and merges them with what it writes; it never overwrites them.
LanguageData.RWL_Conn_Bind: Bind address (127.0.0.1 keeps the bridge on this machine)
LanguageData.RWL_Conn_Token: Bridge token (the agent reads it from bridge.json)
LanguageData.RWL_Conn_RegenWarn: This restarts the bridge with a new token. An agent on another machine needs the new token. The mind inside the mod is not affected.
LanguageData.RWL_Conn_EndpointHelp: The OpenAI-compatible LLM the mod talks to directly. The RimWorldLLM engine is not started in this mode; the key is kept in this setting and in bridge.json.
LanguageData.RWL_Conn_KeyNote: The key is stored in the mod settings and in bridge.json, which only your user account can read. It is never sent through the bridge API.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_Title: Use an engine on another PC on my network
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_PcHelp: The game here talks to the other PC's engine; nothing is downloaded or run on this PC. The other PC keeps its game (or easyEngine) running.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_FindTip: Looks for shared engines on this network and on your Tailscale network, if Tailscale is installed (a few seconds). Pick one and press Connect: the code shown here also shows on the other PC, which presses Allow. Nothing to type.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_NoneFound: No engine answered. On the other PC, turn on "Share this PC's engine on my network" (Model settings, local engine) and keep the game running there. You can also type its address below.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_TypedTip: The engine computer's name or IP address, with :port if it is not 47480 (for example 192.168.1.20 or den-pc:47480).
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_EndpointTip: Asks the URL below whether it is an easyEngine. If the key below already works, it is kept and stored for this engine; otherwise you pair with a code.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_EndpointNotEngine: This endpoint isn't an easyEngine; keep the key typed by hand.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_CodeIntro: Pairing with {0}. This code is on its screen too:
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_CodeCompare: Compare with the code on the engine's screen and press Allow there.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_Reconnecting: Lost the connection to the engine; trying again...
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_Gone: The request ended on {0} (the engine restarted, or another request from this computer replaced it).
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_NotAnEngine: {0} did not answer as an easyEngine. For another server, fill in the fields below by hand.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_NoPairing: {0} needs a key but does not offer pairing. Paste the key it gives (easy-engine token) below.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_StatusTyped: Endpoint typed by hand (not a paired engine).
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_StatusPairAgain: {0} does not accept this game's key. Pair again.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_StatusRevoked: {0} removed this PC. Pair again to use its engine.
LanguageData.RWL_Pair_MsgPairAgain: RimWorldLLM: the engine no longer accepts this game. Pair again in the mod settings (Model).
LanguageData.RWL_Share_Toggle: Share this PC's engine on my network
LanguageData.RWL_Share_ToggleTip: Lets your other PCs with RimWorldLLM use this PC's engine, at home (LAN) or over Tailscale. Each one has to pair first: you compare a code and press Allow here. Off: the engine listens on this PC only.\n\nThe first time, the Windows firewall asks whether easy-engine may use the network: allow it on private networks only. On a Mac, allow incoming connections when asked.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_Exposure: Any device on this network (a cafe's Wi-Fi too) can see this PC's engine name and model; only PCs you Allow can use it.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_StatusOff: Not shared: the engine serves this PC only.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_StatusNoNetwork: Sharing is on, but this PC has no private network up right now (no LAN or Tailscale address). It starts when one is.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_StatusUnsupported: This engine can't share yet. Update RimWorldLLM on this PC.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_RowTip: Click to show this address as a QR code.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_QrTip: Scan with a phone to check the engine answers at {0}. Other PCs find it by themselves.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_WaitingNote: Allow only if the other PC shows the same code. After a Deny, that PC's new requests wait here without a pop-up.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_PairedNone: No PC is paired with this engine yet.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_PairedUnsupported: This engine can't list paired PCs yet. Update RimWorldLLM on this PC.
LanguageData.RWL_Share_PairedError: Couldn't read or change the paired PCs: {0}
LanguageData.RWL_Share_RemoveTip: Takes this PC's access away at once. It has to pair again to use this engine.
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Title: A PC wants to use this engine
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Body: {0} wants to use this PC's engine.
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Compare: Allow only if the other PC shows the same code.
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Changed: It asked again with a new code. Compare again.
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Failed: The engine didn't take the answer. Press Allow or Deny again.
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Allowed: Allowed. {0} can use this PC's engine now.
LanguageData.RWL_PairReq_Gone: The request ended (withdrawn on the other PC, or answered elsewhere).
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_OkFixedBase: Works at {0}. The base URL was updated.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_Paused: Endpoint paused: another program on that machine is using its graphics card. It comes back by itself.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_Loading: The server is up but still loading the model. Try again in a moment.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_Slow: Works, but the reply took {0} ms. Lines may arrive too late.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_ReasoningText: Works, but reasoning text comes back in the output. Turn thinking off on the server.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_BadUrl: That is not a usable http or https URL.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_NothingListening: Nothing is listening there. Check the host, port and that the server is running.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_KeyRejected: The server rejected the API key.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_TokenRequired: The engine needs this game to be paired with it. Pick "An engine on another PC on my network" above and connect.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_TokenInvalid: The engine does not know this key (another engine at this address, or its keys were replaced). Pair again.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_TokenRevoked: The engine's PC removed this PC. Pair again to use it.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_WrongBase: Wrong base URL: no /models there. Did you mean {0}?
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_ModelNotFound: The server has no model called "{0}".
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_Tls: TLS error: the certificate is not trusted, or the server is not speaking https.
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_NotJson: The server answered, but not with an OpenAI-style JSON reply. Is this the right URL?
LanguageData.RWL_Probe_Timeout: No reply in time. The server may be overloaded or still loading.
LanguageData.RWL_Talk_PauseAt: Pause ambient chatter at game speed (0 = never)
LanguageData.RWL_Talk_PauseHelp: At or above this speed the agent stops starting ambient conversations.
LanguageData.RWL_Effects_Help: What a line can do to moods and opinions. Sizes and daily limits are fixed by the mod.
LanguageData.RWL_Events_AgentUrl: Agent dial-out URL (the mod POSTs events here)
LanguageData.RWL_Events_Push: Push events to that URL (they are always kept for GET /events)
LanguageData.RWL_Dreams_EnableTip: A sleeping colonist may get a short surreal dream cloud drawn from the day's memories and thoughts. Turning this off also stops the falling-asleep events.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_Help: The engine writes fresh text for single things when they are made: an artwork's title and description, an epitaph on a grave, a book's title and blurb, a line in the social log. It uses what was going on at the time (who made it, their mood, the weather, recent events), so the text fits that one thing. The game's own text shows until ours is written, in the background when the engine is idle; nothing waits for it.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_Enable: Write flavour text for single things
LanguageData.RWL_Text_EnableTip: Turn off to keep the game's own text everywhere. Texts already written are kept in the save and show again when you turn it back on.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_ArtTip: New art made by colonists, sarcophagus plates, and any artwork the first time you look at it.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_GravesTip: An epitaph for the person buried, from who they were and how they died. Shown in the grave's inspect pane.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_BooksTip: Books written in the colony, and any book the first time you open its info card. The book's effects are unchanged.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_SocialTip: Lines in the social log. Romance lines and lines that report an outcome keep the game's text.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_CombatTip: Shots fired, misses, dodges and deflections. Hits keep the game's text, which names the wound. Off by default: fights make many lines.
LanguageData.RWL_Text_Vanilla: Only things that get a written text change; everything else keeps the game's text. Names of people, factions and places, quests and letters always stay the game's.
LanguageData.RWL_Art_EnableTip: When a colonist finishes an artwork, the engine writes a short description from the colony's history. It replaces the game's generated text on the info card; the title stays. Turn off to see the game's own text again.
LanguageData.RWL_Bubbles_Colors: Give each pawn their own bubble colour
LanguageData.RWL_Recap_Enable: Recap when a save is loaded
LanguageData.RWL_Recap_EnableTip: After you load a save, a letter titled "Previously on ..." gives a three-line recap of the colony's chronicle. It never pauses the game.
LanguageData.RWL_Adult_EnableTip: Off: romance and affection are fine, anything sexual fades to black. On: explicit sexual content between adult colonists. Never involving anyone under 18, in either setting.
LanguageData.RWL_Adult_ConfirmText: Turn on adult content? This allows explicit sexual content between adult colonists; never involving anyone under 18.
LanguageData.RWL_Wants_EnableTip: In quiet moments a pawn may decide to seek someone out for a chat or to keep clear of someone for a while. Only ever small social moves; anything more important interrupts them.
LanguageData.RWL_Wants_AvoidHours: How long a pawn avoids someone: {0} game hours
LanguageData.RWL_Thoughts_Show: Show pawn thoughts on the map
LanguageData.RWL_Thoughts_ShowTip: Short thoughts appear as faint cloud balloons over a pawn who is not speaking. The full text stays in the Mind tab. Diary entries never appear on the map.
LanguageData.RWL_Thoughts_Opacity: Thought cloud opacity: {0}% of bubble opacity
LanguageData.RWL_Thoughts_PerPawn: Seconds between thought clouds over one pawn
LanguageData.RWL_Adv_FixedToken: Fixed shared token (blank = a random token each run)
LanguageData.RWL_Adv_FixedTokenHelp: Needed when the agent runs on another machine. Anyone with the token can read colony state and make pawns speak.
LanguageData.RWL_Adv_DebugNeedsDev: The debug window needs development mode.
LanguageData.RWL_Debug_State: Bridge: {0}. Requests waiting for the game thread: {1}.
LanguageData.RWL_Debug_Stores: Op-id store: {0} remembered. Event ring: {1} kept, last seq {2}. Talk queue: {3} waiting.
LanguageData.RWL_Debug_TestHelp: Queues a talk request for the pawn; the mind picks it up from GET /talk and answers with POST /say.
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_AutoStart: Start the local engine with the game
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_AutoStartTip: Launches (or attaches to) the RimWorldLLM engine when RimWorld starts. It stops when the game exits.
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_SourceLocalTip: RimWorldLLM downloads and runs a model that fits your graphics card and memory.
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_SourcePc: An engine on another PC on my network
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_SourcePcTip: Use the engine of another PC that has RimWorldLLM too (at home, or on your Tailscale network). That PC turns on "Share this PC's engine on my network"; this one finds it and pairs with a code.
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_SourceOwnTip: Use any OpenAI-compatible server you already run (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, a cloud API).
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_LocalNote: The engine picks how many lines can be written at once and how much each can remember, from your free graphics memory. It makes room for the game and grows back when there is room.
LanguageData.RWL_Eng_NoAnswer: The engine was started but did not answer. See its log in the setup window.
LanguageData.RWL_First_Text: RimWorldLLM can set up a local model that runs on your own computer: it checks your graphics card and memory, picks a model that fits, and downloads it. Or you can use a GGUF model file or an endpoint you already have.
LanguageData.RWL_Setup_Title: RimWorldLLM: set up a local model
LanguageData.RWL_Setup_NoGpu: No usable graphics card found: models will run on the processor, slowly.
LanguageData.RWL_Setup_ImportHelp: For models that are not downloadable: type the full path of a .gguf file you already have. It is checked and copied into the engine.
LanguageData.RWL_Setup_Shape: Running now: {0} lines at once, {1} memory each, {2} expert layers on the processor, {3} cache, about {4} of graphics memory.
LanguageData.RWL_Fallback_DefaultNote: Smallest model: expect repeated lines and weaker understanding of what was said.
LanguageData.RWL_Fallback_RowWarning: Warning: this is the smallest model, kept only as a fallback. {0}
LanguageData.RWL_Fallback_ConfirmText:
This is the smallest model, kept only as a fallback for computers that cannot run a larger one. {0}
Use it anyway?
LanguageData.RWL_Fallback_StatusLine: Warning: the smallest (fallback) model is in use. {0}
LanguageData.RWL_Fallback_MessageText: RimWorldLLM is using its smallest model. Speech will be simpler and may repeat. To change it, open Options, Mod settings, RimWorldLLM, then "Set up / Change model...".
LanguageData.RWL_Starter_MessageText: RimWorldLLM is talking with a small starter model while the full model downloads. Speech will be simpler until it switches over by itself.
LanguageData.RWL_Starter_ReadyText: RimWorldLLM switched to the full model ({0}).
LanguageData.RWL_Starter_StatusLine: Starter model: simpler speech while the full model downloads ({0}%).
LanguageData.RWL_Starter_StatusLineVerifying: Starter model: the full model has downloaded and is being checked ({0}%).
LanguageData.RWL_Starter_StatusLineNoPct: Starter model: simpler speech while the full model downloads.
LanguageData.RWL_Fallback_HideSetting: Don't warn about the small model again
LanguageData.RWL_Camera_Tip: The camera follows the most interesting colonist on this map, like a TV director. Moving the camera yourself pauses it for ten seconds. You can also bind a key under Options, Keyboard, RimWorldLLM.
LanguageData.RWL_Camera_AllowedTip: Shows the director camera button in the Voices window and enables its key binding.
LanguageData.RWL_Camera_OnAtStart: Start each game with the director camera on
LanguageData.RWL_Camera_OnAtStartTip: Off by default: a following camera is intrusive. Any camera control you use pauses it for ten seconds.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_Tip: Watch mode: the camera cuts between what is happening in the colony by itself (raids, fights, births, weddings, deaths and more) and says what it is showing in the chat. Moving the camera yourself pauses it for a while.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_ModeTip: The camera cuts between colony events by itself. Also a button beside the Narrator plays eye, and a key under Options, Keyboard, RimWorldLLM. Off by default.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_Captions: Watch mode: write a "Camera:" line to the chat for each shot
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_CaptionsTip: One short line per shot of interest, at most one every twelve seconds (four for urgent events). Filler shots get none.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_PauseSec: Watch mode: seconds the camera stays still after you move it
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_PauseSecTip: Moving, zooming or edge-scrolling the camera pauses the director for this long.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_Zoom: Watch mode: zoom for each shot
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_ZoomTip: Close for meals, deathbeds and art, middle for work, wide for raids and battles, always inside your own zoom limits. Your zoom comes back when watch mode turns off.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_SelectFollowed: Watch mode: select the pawn the camera follows
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_SelectFollowedTip: Off by default: selecting opens the inspect pane, which covers part of the screen. Selecting never drafts or changes anything else.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_PaceTip: How long the camera stays on each shot and how soon it may show the same pawn or scene again. Calm: long shots, five minutes before a repeat. Lively: short shots, two and a half minutes.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_Scenes: Watch mode: everyday scenes to show when nothing else is happening
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_ScenesTip: Events (raids, deaths, births and more) always come first. Scenes fill the quiet stretches.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_SceneWorkTip: Fields, kitchen, building, workshop and mining; also prisoners being talked to and animals being tamed.
LanguageData.RWL_Watch_SceneRomanceTip: Adults only, and never in bed.
LanguageData.RWL_FileBrowser_UpTip: Go to the folder above this one.
LanguageData.RWL_FileBrowser_RootsTip: Show the drives and top-level places on this computer.
LanguageData.RWL_FileBrowser_SelectTip: Use the highlighted .gguf file. Double-clicking a file does the same.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Enabled: Turns RimWorldLLM off or on without removing the mod. Nothing is said while it is off.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_LlmUrl: The address of an OpenAI-compatible server, for example http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_LlmModel: The model name your server expects. Leave blank if it serves just one.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_LlmKey: Only needed for servers that ask for a key. It is kept in your settings file, not shared.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_StatusCard: Green means the model is ready, amber means it is busy, red means something went wrong.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_ChangeModel: Pick a different model. Your computer is checked first, so only ones that fit are offered.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_UseOwnFile: Use a .gguf model file you already have on this computer. It is used where it is, never copied.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Test: Sends a tiny test message to the model and shows how long it took.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_HideFallback: Stops the notice about the small stand-in model.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_DeleteOld: Frees disk space by deleting the model you switched away from.
LanguageData.RWL_Prev_Offer: You switched away from {0}. It still takes {1} of disk space.
LanguageData.RWL_Prev_Confirm: Delete {0} and free {1}? You can download it again later.
LanguageData.RWL_Switch_Line: Downloading {0}: {1}%. The current model keeps talking until it is ready.
LanguageData.RWL_Switch_LineNoPct: Downloading {0}. The current model keeps talking until it is ready.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Frequency: How often colonists speak up on their own. 1.0 is normal, 0 is silent unless something happens.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_EffectsOff: What colonists say never changes moods or opinions.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_EffectsLight: Spoken lines nudge moods and opinions at half strength.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_EffectsNormal: Spoken lines nudge moods and opinions at full (still small, capped) strength.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_AvoidHours: How many game hours a colonist keeps avoiding someone after saying they want to.
LanguageData.RWL_Events_Help: Which happenings are allowed to start a spoken line.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Injury: Colonists react when someone gets hurt.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_MentalBreak: Colonists react when someone has a mental break.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_LevelUp: Colonists comment when someone gains a skill level.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Tend: Colonists comment when a patient is treated.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Social: Colonists comment on chats, insults and romance attempts.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Lodger: Colonists react to guests and lodgers arriving or leaving.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Prisoner: Colonists react to prisoners being captured, recruited or freed.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Thought: Colonists talk about strong thoughts and moods.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Sleep: Lets sleeping colonists dream. Dreams show as clouds.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Firsts: Colonists remark on things they see for the first time.
LanguageData.RWL_EvTip_Gatherings: Colonists talk during meals, parties, weddings, rituals and speeches.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_BubblesShow: Shows what colonists say as bubbles over their heads.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_BubblesColors: Each colonist gets a bubble colour of their own.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_BubbleStyle: Round comic balloons with tails, or plain boxes.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Lettering: Writes bubble text in capital letters, like a comic.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_BubbleDuration: How many seconds a bubble stays on screen.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_ThoughtOpacity: How see-through thought clouds are compared with speech bubbles.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_ThoughtPerPawn: The least number of seconds between two thought clouds from the same colonist.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_ThoughtGlobal: The least number of seconds between two thought clouds anywhere on the map.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_PanSpeed: How quickly the director camera moves to its subject.
LanguageData.RWL_Content_AgeGate: The age gate is always on: nobody under 18 appears in anything romantic or sexual. It cannot be turned off.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_AgeGate: A fixed safety rule built into the mod. No setting changes it.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_Texts: Written texts in this game, stored (+ waiting): {0}
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_Help: Where the engine keeps its models and files, and how much room they take.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_NoEngine: The engine is not running, so its files cannot be listed. Start it from the Model tab.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_Failed: The engine did not answer in time. Try Refresh.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_StorageFolder: Everything the engine downloads or installs lives here.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_OpenFolder: Opens that folder in your file manager.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_ModelInUse: This model is answering right now, so it cannot be deleted.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_ModelDelete: Deletes this model file to free disk space. You can download it again later.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_DeleteConfirm: Delete {0} ({1})? You can download it again later.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_YourFileNote: Your own GGUF file is never touched: it stays where you keep it.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_RemoveAll: Stops the engine and deletes everything it downloaded. Your settings stay.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_RemoveConfirm:
This stops the engine and deletes the downloaded models, the engine runtime and unfinished downloads. {0} of disk space comes back.
Your RimWorldLLM settings are kept, and so is any GGUF file you chose yourself. Afterwards, Set up starts over from the beginning.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_RemoveMemory: Also delete RimWorldLLM's memory and logs ({0})
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_RemoveMemory: The mind's own folder: what colonists remember and its logs (the mind pauses while it is deleted). Leave this off to keep them for a later reinstall.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_MemoryDeleted: RimWorldLLM's memory and logs were deleted ({0}).
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_MemoryNone: RimWorldLLM had no memory or logs to delete.
LanguageData.RWL_Storage_MemoryRefused: RimWorldLLM's memory and logs in {0} were not deleted: {1}
LanguageData.RWL_Gpu_HostAndModel: Game on {0} · {1}: {2} free for the model
LanguageData.RWL_Gpu_Shared: Game and model share {0}: {1} free for the model
LanguageData.RWL_Gpu_Cpu: No graphics card in use: the model runs on the processor
LanguageData.RWL_Adv_Help: For people running their own agent or tools. Most players never need this tab.
LanguageData.RWL_Adv_OpenWarning: Anyone on your network can read colony state and make colonists speak. Set a shared token below, or bind to 127.0.0.1.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Port: The port the in-game bridge listens on. Change it only if another program already uses 9765.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Bind: 127.0.0.1 keeps the bridge on this computer. Anything else opens it to your network.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Token: The password an outside agent uses to talk to the bridge. It is written to bridge.json for you.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_AgentUrl: If you run your own agent, the mod posts colony events to this address.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Push: Sends colony events to the agent address above. Events are always kept for the bridge.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_Restart: Stops and starts the bridge again, for example after changing the port.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_OpenPage: Opens the engine page in your web browser.
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_Title: RimWorldLLM: use my own GGUF file
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_Note: The file stays where it is. RimWorldLLM reads it in place and never copies, moves or deletes it.
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_NoEngine: The engine is not running yet. It starts with the game; wait a moment or open the Model tab.
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_Facts: Architecture {0}, {1} parameters, {2}, trained for {3} tokens of context, {4} on disk.
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_NoTemplate: This file has no built-in chat format. It may answer badly.
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_Estimated: This size estimate is a careful guess from the file header.
LanguageData.RWL_Custom_StatusMissing: Your file {0} was not found at {1}. Pick another file or stop using it.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_CustomPath: Type the full path, or use Browse.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_CustomCheck: Reads the file header and tells you if it fits your computer. Nothing is changed.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_CustomUse: Starts serving this file. The previous model stays on disk.
LanguageData.RWL_Tip_CustomClear: Goes back to the last downloaded model. Your file is not deleted.
LanguageData.RWL_Setup_OwnFileHelp: Have a GGUF file already? Use it where it is, without copying it.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_Help: When "Narrator plays" is on (the eye icon at the bottom right, or its key), the narrator runs the colony and you can still act and talk to it. These settings limit what it may do.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_MayPause: The narrator may pause for emergencies
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_MayPauseTip: Lets the narrator pause the game when something urgent happens, even though it does not control the speed.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_ControlsSpeed: The narrator controls the game speed
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_MayLook: Narrator may look at the screen
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_MayLookTip: The narrator may take a picture of the map (never the interface) when planning the base. Used only when the model supports images.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_ExecutePrisonersTip: Off: the narrator never orders a prisoner executed. On: it may set a prisoner to be executed, always with a reason you can read.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_SlaughterPets: The narrator may slaughter named pets
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_SlaughterPetsTip: Off: the narrator may slaughter only unnamed, unbonded colony animals. On: it may also slaughter animals with a name or a bond.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_SlowForCombat: The narrator slows the game for fights
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_SlowForCombatTip: On: when a fight starts the narrator sets normal speed, and puts your speed back when it ends (unless you changed it meanwhile). Works even when the narrator does not control the speed.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_CommentaryTip: While Narrator plays is on, the narrator adds a short documentary line at big moments (raids, deaths, births, weddings, masterworks, ship parts) and one recap line a game day, when its slot is free. The lines are under the Story filter.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_AnswerDialogs: Answer popups when the narrator plays
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_AnswerDialogsTip: While Narrator plays is on, the narrator answers choice windows and letters (joiners, ransom demands, quests, naming, growth moments). One it leaves open past the timeout gets the safe default: accept joiners and visitors, decline ransoms and quests, a fallback name, the harmless button.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_DialogTimeout: Seconds before a popup gets the safe default
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_DialogTimeoutTip: Real seconds, not game time: popups pause the game. Default 90.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_ControlsSpeedTip: Off: your speed is respected. On: the narrator may pause, unpause and change the speed.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_ImplantGenesTip: Off: the narrator may assemble xenogerms but never implants one. On: it may set a grown colonist to receive a xenogerm, always with a plan you can read. Never children or prisoners.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_Heartbeat: The narrator looks at the colony every {0} game hours
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_HeartbeatTip: How often the narrator wakes up on its own to look over the colony, in game hours. It also wakes when you chat or something important happens.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_Autosave: Rotating autosave while the narrator plays
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_AutosaveTip: Only when the game's own autosave is off: the mod saves as RWL-Narrator-1, -2 ... and rotates, never touching other saves. If the game's autosave is on, it does the job and this stays quiet.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_AutosaveDaysTip: How often the mod's autosave runs, in game days. It waits while a window is open or a raid is on (but not for ever).
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_AutosaveKeepTip: How many RWL-Narrator saves rotate. The oldest is overwritten; saves the mod did not make are never touched.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_TradeTip: Lets the narrator buy and sell with visiting traders and settlements, within the limits below. In advisor mode only when you ask.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_CaravansTip: Lets the narrator send colonists out on caravans to trade or work quests. It never sends everyone, nor the best doctor or only cook unless you ask.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_TradeMaxDealTip: The most silver one trade may move. Bigger deals are refused.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_TradeMaxDayTip: The most silver the narrator may move in trades per day.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_TradeDealsPerDayTip: The most trades the narrator may make in a day.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_KeepMedicineTip: The narrator never sells medicine below this many.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_KeepFoodDaysTip: The narrator never sells food that would leave the colony with fewer days than this.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_NeverSellTip: Item names the narrator must never sell, separated by commas. For example: Mortar shell, Neutroamine.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_CaravanMaxPawnsTip: The most colonists the narrator may send on one caravan.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartModeTip: Only while the narrator plays. Ask: a window offers a new colony on this world, a new world, or stopping. Restart by itself: new colonists on this world if the game allows, else a new world; the lost world is saved once under a new name first and nothing is ever deleted. Click to change.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartText: {0} has no colonists left. The narrator can carry on with a new colony.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartSameNo: The game cannot send new colonists right now.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartNewBtn: New world (this one is saved first)
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartAuto: The colony is lost. Starting over in {0} seconds.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartSame: Starting a new colony on this world.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartNew: Saving the lost world, then starting a new one.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_RestartSaveFailed: Could not save the lost world, so it is being kept as it is. Not restarting.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_SwitchTip: Narrator plays: the narrator runs the colony; you can still act and talk to it.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_ChatHint: Talk to the narrator, or @Name to talk to a colonist (Enter sends, Esc closes)
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_UndoTip: Takes back the narrator's last placing action: its blueprints and frames are cancelled, its designations, zones and bills removed. Finished buildings stay. In the chat, type /undo or /undo 3.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_ShowTip: The chat log stays on screen, translucent, at the side. Off: it shows only while you type (Enter).
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_RightTip: Off: the left side, next to the resources list. On: the right side, left of the date and alerts.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_MediumTip: Uses the medium font for the chat panel instead of the small one.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_OpacityTip: How dark the panel's background is while the mouse is elsewhere. Under the mouse it is nearly opaque.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_MoveHelp: Drag the chat panel by its top strip (shown under the mouse) and resize it from the bottom-right corner. "On the right" is only where it starts until you move it.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_ResetPosTip: Forget where you dragged the panel; it goes back to the side chosen above, at its default size.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_FTalkTip: Your lines and what the colonists say.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_FThoughtsTip: Colonists' thoughts, dreams and diary entries.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_FNarratorTip: The narrator's lines and system notes.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_FActionsTip: What the narrator did, and what it was not allowed to do.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_FStoryTip: Chronicle entries, recaps and artwork descriptions.
LanguageData.RWL_Chat_ChipTip: Click to show or hide these lines.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_OrdersEmpty: No standing orders. Add one, for example: always keep 20 meals.
LanguageData.RWL_Viv_Log: What the narrator did and why
